data.content_ref: inline:Reformulate the skeptical semantics as a finite two-player dialectical game: a conjecture is accepted iff the proponent has a winning strategy in a DAG game where opponent attacks are answered by defeat trees rooted at committed roots; solve by backward induction in polynomial time. This preserves determinism and polynomial cost, makes reinstatement a natural game-theoretic consequence, and enforces committed-root validity by construction, but it may be criticized for being a notational variant of the fixpoint rather than an expansion.
